title: Two ways to sense
hook: One way of sensing does not rule out another.

knows: Animals have body structures and life histories.
doesNotKnow: Separate echolocation from the assumption of blindness.

misconception: A familiar animal feature always has the first explanation that comes to mind.
objective: Separate echolocation from the assumption of blindness.

claims.text: Many bats echolocate. What follows about their ability to see? The diagram shows two separate channels: light can reach eyes and sound can return to ears. Many bats can see as well as use echolocation. Knowing that an animal uses one sense does not prove the absence of another.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: National Park Service, bats, https://www.nps.gov/subjects/bats/index.htm

claims.text: The diagram and its labels are schematic, not to scale and not an observation. Sensory channels · schematic
An animal detects returning sounds. Can that fact alone show it has no vision? Using sound does not by itself tell us whether an animal can see.
